messages:
maya: Customer on prod complaining about SSE streams cutting out with partial payloads. Happens ~30s into long chat sessions, only when traffic goes through Cloudflare + our ALB. Not reproducible when hitting origin directly.

maya: Example from customer: client gets a partial final chunk and then connection closed, app retries and resumes but they see duplicated tokens and billing spike.

maya: From their client logs: 
```
[INFO] SSE stream started
...tokens...
<partial chunk: '\\u003cresponse-truncated\\u003e'>
[WARN] connection closed by remote host
```

ajay: thanks — does the origin log show anything? any early FINs or proxy responses?

maya: origin app logs show normal keepalives, no app-level error. nginx access log shows 200 then connection: close shortly after. No 502/504.

ben: couple of quick hypotheses:
- ALB idle timeout or connection reassign due to stickiness/cookie rotation causing connection to be reset mid-stream.
- Cloudflare edge buffering or WAF/worker closing origin connection early when session affinity changes.
- nginx proxy_buffering/gzip combining chunks and then ALB doing half-close.

maya: repro steps I gave them to try: hit origin directly (works). hit through ALB only (intermittent but mostly ok). through Cloudflare+ALB (fails consistently).

jess-cs: customer says they have sticky sessions on ALB for other reasons, and rotate a session cookie every 20s for auth refresh.

ajay: interesting — cookie rotation while a long-lived connection is open can cause the ALB to re-evaluate targets (health checks, or re-stick to a new target) and that can lead to an early FIN. Could explain ~30s window.

ben: can you ask them to run a minimal repro that streams a comment every 10s so we can see where the break happens? e.g. server SSE sending:
```
while true; do echo -e "data: heartbeat\n\n"; sleep 10; done | some-sse-server
```
and curl from client:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://edge.example.com/sse/stream
```
(make sure -N so curl doesn't buffer)

maya: they ran that. Observed: last heartbeat appears, then within 2s connection reset from remote.

ajay: ask them to tcpdump the origin-facing interface to confirm origin sees FIN from ALB or sees keepalive drop. Example tcpdump filter: `tcpdump -w sse.pcap -s 0 host <edge-ip> and port 443` and around timestamp inspect RST/FIN flags.

maya: customer sent pcap. I looked — after the last chunk from origin we see a FIN from the ALB immediately (client-side side still open).

ben: that strongly points to the ALB or Cloudflare deciding to close the origin connection. Two action items:
1) Temporarily disable ALB stickiness / cookie affinity for that target group and repro.
2) Increase ALB idle timeout and make sure Cloudflare origin timeout isn't lower (Cloudflare default is 100s but workers or custom settings could be lower).

maya: also tried toggling `proxy_buffering off;` in nginx for that endpoint and restart, but still reproduced through Cloudflare+ALB. Through ALB only, toggling buffer helped.

ajay: that fits — nginx buffering plus ALB stickiness+cookie rotation cause timing edge. When Cloudflare sits in front, it may multiplex or reuse connections to origin differently and the cookie swap triggers a connection close.

ben: other mitigations while they investigate:
- Send periodic SSE comment heartbeats more frequently (every 10s) so clients can detect and recover gracefully.
- Add a short-lived Connection: keep-alive header and `Keep-Alive: timeout=120, max=100` at origin to encourage longer origin connection lifetime.
- Turn off ALB stickiness for that route OR make session cookie rotation align with SSE TTL.

maya: customer applied disabling stickiness on a test ALB and retested — streams stayed open >5m, no partial chunks.

jess-cs: customer confirms disabling stickiness is a workable short-term fix. They want guidance on long-term: they need session affinity for other endpoints.

ben: long-term options:
- Move SSE endpoint to a dedicated target group that has stickiness disabled. Keep the rest behind sticky TG.
- Use Cloudflare Workers to pin origin connection via consistent routing or use a separate subdomain for streaming with different Cloudflare settings.
- Avoid rotating auth cookies while a stream is open; use a separate short token refresh mechanism for streaming sockets.

ajay: can we add a note to docs: "SSE best practice: avoid ALB stickiness + cookie rotation; prefer dedicated non-sticky target for streaming or use short client heartbeats." I'll file a quick doc PR.

maya: customer also asked about billing noise from duplicate/resume tokens. I suggested adding idempotency at application layer for tokens and server-side dedupe on resumed sessions.

ingress-bot: autolog — created INCIDENT-7893 for "SSE: ALB session dissociation causes early FIN with Cloudflare in front" and attached pcap and logs.

maya: next steps for support: 1) share recommended mitigations with customer (disable stickiness for streaming TG + add heartbeats) 2) offer to help move streaming to a dedicated subdomain + Cloudflare zone to isolate settings 3) doc update PR from ajay.

jess-cs: customer happy with plan, will schedule a config window. thanks team :thumbsup: 

ben: follow-up — let's add an internal runbook entry with diagnostic tcpdump flags, steps to check ALB target cookie rotations, and a checklist for Cloudflare origin timeout settings.

maya: I'll draft the runbook and link INCIDENT-7893.

ben: nice catch. closing thread after runbook PR.
